body: Build the transcript importer for Claude Code sessions so recall works across projects.

Decision: we store only text blocks and drop tool traffic, because tool output is what makes grep useless here.

Should the importer also read the nested subagent transcripts?
No, never import the subagent transcripts, they are machine chatter. Let's keep the importer to top-level session files only.

The importer is in and the tests pass. Nested transcripts are skipped as agreed.

Next: wire the enrich stages so the imported events get entities and episodes.
Add the Sense connector import for staffing exports and a dashboard for it.

I'll use the existing connector slot pattern instead of a new module tree, so the dashboard reuses the connector cards. Sense has no public API, so phase one is import only.

Do you want the inbound endpoint gated behind a feature flag?

Edit {ROOT}/onekit/src/connectors/sense.ts
Edit {ROOT}/onekit/src/connectors/sense.ts
Bash git commit -m "feat: sense connector import"
Now build the handoff packet compiler on top of the imported sessions. Use the contract in docs/handoff and go with whitespace tokens for the budget.

The plan is to extract sessions by header, then render sections in contract order under the token budget.

Don't cite screen text as if the user typed it; only transcript events carry a role.
Agreed. Also we'll always end every cited line with the event id so it can be checked. Do not use an LLM for extraction.

Extraction and rendering are in place and the budget test passes at 128 and 600 tokens. Is the Sources section supposed to list uncited ids too?

Remaining: the migration is registered but the CLI arm is not wired yet, so `mci-agent handoff` still prints usage. Then run clippy.
